<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par119 />''above'' (so also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=39}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=25|hidebook=1}}, not ''from above''). These adverbs of place, however, may become prepositions by the addition of {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מִחוּץ לְ|translate=outside as regards}} ..., i.e. ''outside of something'', in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=13}} even after a transitive verb of motion; {{GHGheb|text=מִתַּ֫חַת לְ|translate=below as regards}} ..., i.e. ''under something'' (cf. {{GHGheb|text=עַד־מִתַּ֫חַת לְ|translate=until they came under}} ..., {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=7|verse=11}}), {{GHGheb|text=מֵעַל לְ|translate=over something}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=לְבַד}} prop. ''in separation''; {{GHGheb|text=לְבַד מִן־|translate=in separation from}}, i.e. ''apart from, besides''. Only rarely in such a case is the {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} omitted for the sake of brevity, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=26|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=מִתַּ֫חַת מַיִם|translate=beneath}} the ''waters''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=3|verse=28}} ({{GHGheb|text=מֵעַל־}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|d}}
2. Real combinations of prepositions (each retaining its full force) occur—

(''a'') With {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}}, in {{GHGheb|text=מֵאַחַר}}, {{GHGheb|text=מֵאַֽחֲרֵי}} (see above) ''from behind'' something; {{GHGheb|text=מֵאֵת}} and {{GHGheb|text=מֵעִם|translate=from with}} (see above); {{GHGheb|text=מִבֵּין}} or {{GHGheb|text=מִבֵּינוֹת|translate=from between}} something (with motion in either direction, see e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=10}}); {{GHGheb|text=מִלִּפְנֵי|translate=from before}} (see above); sometimes also {{GHGheb|text=מִמּוּל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=5|verse=8}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=מֵעַל־|translate=from upon}}, i.e. ''off from''; {{GHGheb|text=מִתַּ֫חַת|translate=away from under}} (see footnote 2 on p. 377).

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|e}}
(''b'') With {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־}}, in {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־אַֽחֲרֵי|translate=to behind}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־בֵּינוֹת|translate=to between}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־מִבֵּית לְ|translate=forth between}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=11|verse=15}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־מִחוּץ לְ|translate=forth without}}, i.e. ''out in front of'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=5|verse=3}}; {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־תַּ֫חַת|translate=down under}}.<ref>Also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=21|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־תַּ֫חַת}} by a pregnant construction is virtually dependent on the idea of ''coming into'', contained in the preceding {{GHGheb|text=אֵין־}}.</ref>—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=5|verse=5}} the two prepositions of motion are combined in a peculiarly pregnant construction, {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־מִצִּנִּים}} (he goes thither and takes it) ''out of the thorns'', i.e. he taketh it ''even out of the thorns'', but the text is hardly correct.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|f}}
'''3.''' A general view of the union of certain verbs, or whole classes of verbs, with particular prepositions, especially in explanation of certain idioms and pregnant expressions.<ref>A summary of ''all'' the relations and senses in which a preposition may be used, belongs not to the Grammar but to the Lexicon.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|g}}
(''a'') {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֱלֵי}})<ref>Cf. Mitchell, ‘The preposition ''el'',’ in the ''Journal of the Society of Biblical Literature and Exegesis'', 1888, p. 143 ff., and especially A. Noordtzij, ''Het hebreeuwsche voorzetsel'' {{GHGheb|text=אל}}, Leiden, 1896, a thorough examination of its uses, and especially of the relation between {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־}} and {{GHGheb|text=עַל־}}.</ref> ''towards'', properly an expression of ''motion'' or at least ''direction'' towards something (either in the sense of ''up to''={{GHGheb|text=עַד}}, or ''into''={{GHGheb|text=אֶל־תּוֹךְ}}), is used after verbs not only in answer to the question ''whither?'' but by a specially pregnant construction, in answer to the question ''where?'' e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=41|verse=12}} ''they''<section end=par119 /><noinclude>
